title: IBMP Pain Medicine — Set A

questions.stem: After a pinprick, a patient perceives an immediate, well-localised sharp pain before a slower burning sensation. Which fibres primarily carry the first sensation?

options.text: Preganglionic autonomic B fibres
Unmyelinated C fibres
Thinly myelinated A-delta fibres
Large myelinated A-alpha motor fibres

scoring.explanation: A-delta fibres carry fast, localised nociceptive signals; C fibres carry slower signals.

questions.stem: Repeated nociceptive input increases the responsiveness of neurons within the dorsal horn, including responses to previously subthreshold input. What process does this describe?

options.text: Central sensitisation
Wallerian degeneration
Peripheral nerve conduction block
Descending inhibition

scoring.explanation: The defining change is increased responsiveness within the central nervous system.

questions.stem: Light clothing brushing a painful area produces pain, although the same contact is comfortable elsewhere. What is this finding called?

options.text: Hyperalgesia
Paresthesia
Hypoesthesia
Allodynia

scoring.explanation: Allodynia refers to pain provoked by ordinarily non-painful stimulation.

questions.stem: A clinician records a patient's pain intensity as 7/10. Which additional assessment is most useful for judging the wider impact of persistent pain?

options.text: The number of analgesic brands previously prescribed
The number of abnormalities in an imaging report alone
The patient's height and dominant hand alone
Interference with sleep, activity and participation

scoring.explanation: Intensity should be supplemented by functional and psychosocial assessment.

questions.stem: A patient with chronic primary pain avoids all movement because they believe any discomfort means new injury. Which approach best addresses this barrier?

options.text: Recommend indefinite rest while repeating unchanged investigations
Explore the belief and agree a paced, graded return to meaningful activity
Delay rehabilitation until every pain sensation has disappeared
Confirm that all pain during movement represents tissue injury

scoring.explanation: A collaborative plan can address fear and support safe participation.

questions.stem: An adult with decision-making capacity declines an elective pain procedure after discussing its benefits, risks and alternatives. What is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Respect the decision, document it and discuss acceptable alternatives
Withhold all further pain care until the patient agrees
Treat the refusal as evidence of impaired capacity
Proceed if a relative signs the consent form instead

scoring.explanation: A capacitated patient may decline an elective intervention; consent is an informed dialogue.

questions.stem: After explaining a new analgesic plan, which action best checks whether the clinician has communicated clearly?

options.text: Assume understanding if the patient has previously used pain medicines
Ask the patient to explain the plan and key precautions in their own words
Ask the patient to memorise the medicine leaflet verbatim
Ask only whether the patient understands the prescription

scoring.explanation: Teach-back checks understanding through the patient's own explanation.

questions.stem: A patient with chronic kidney disease and recent dehydration requests oral ibuprofen. Which adverse effect is of particular concern?

options.text: Further renal impairment from reduced renal prostaglandin activity
Permanent suppression of pancreatic insulin release
Direct irreversible blockade of skeletal neuromuscular transmission
Acute opioid withdrawal from mu-receptor antagonism

scoring.explanation: Renal prostaglandin inhibition can compromise kidney function in susceptible patients.

questions.stem: A patient takes paracetamol tablets and an over-the-counter cold preparation that also contains paracetamol. What is the key medication-safety concern?

options.text: The second preparation reliably protects against liver toxicity
Unrecognised duplication can produce a hepatotoxic total dose
Combination products prevent paracetamol absorption completely
Only prescription paracetamol contributes to the daily total

scoring.explanation: All paracetamol-containing products contribute to cumulative exposure and overdose risk.

questions.stem: Before initiating gabapentin in an older patient with neuropathic pain, which factor is especially important when selecting the dose and dosing interval?

options.text: Hepatic enzyme induction alone
Serum albumin alone
Renal function
Body weight without renal assessment

scoring.explanation: Gabapentin is renally cleared, so impaired renal function requires dose adjustment.

questions.stem: An adult has painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy and no contraindication to the options listed. Which medicine is an established initial treatment option?

options.text: Codeine
Prednisolone
Diazepam
Duloxetine

scoring.explanation: Duloxetine is one guideline-supported initial option for this neuropathic pain context.

questions.stem: A patient receiving an opioid is also taking a benzodiazepine. Which combined adverse effect requires particular attention?

options.text: Loss of all opioid analgesic effect through receptor blockade
Sedation and respiratory depression
Reliable reversal of opioid-related constipation
Reduced risk of falls through improved coordination

scoring.explanation: Concurrent central nervous system depressants increase overdose and respiratory risk.

questions.stem: A stable patient receiving long-term opioids for chronic non-cancer pain has no immediate life-threatening toxicity. A review finds that risks now outweigh benefits. What is the preferred approach?

options.text: Agree an individualised, supported reduction plan and optimise other care
Increase the dose automatically to prevent any future discomfort
Stop treatment abruptly without discussing withdrawal or follow-up
Discharge the patient solely because a taper may be needed

scoring.explanation: Absent an urgent safety threat, avoid abrupt cessation and use a collaborative taper.

questions.stem: Before starting an opioid for chronic non-cancer pain, which plan best supports responsible prescribing?

options.text: Use a signed agreement instead of clinical assessment and monitoring
Promise indefinite continuation regardless of function or harms
Agree measurable goals, assess risks, explain precautions and arrange review
Use pain intensity as the only follow-up measure and omit adverse-effect review

scoring.explanation: Opioid care requires goals, risk assessment and ongoing benefit-harm review.

questions.stem: Which presentation is the best match for considering an epidural injection of local anaesthetic and steroid under NICE NG59?

options.text: Neurogenic claudication due to central canal stenosis
Acute, severe sciatica after clinical assessment
Chronic non-specific axial back pain without sciatica
Asymptomatic lumbar degenerative findings on MRI

scoring.explanation: NICE identifies acute severe sciatica as a context in which an epidural may be considered.

questions.stem: A patient is being assessed for radiofrequency treatment of suspected lumbar facet-mediated pain. Which finding most directly supports proceeding with a medial branch pathway?

options.text: A positive screening questionnaire without examination
Facet degeneration on imaging without a matching clinical assessment
Relief after an unrelated peripheral joint injection
A clinically meaningful response to a properly performed diagnostic medial branch block

scoring.explanation: Diagnostic medial branch response is used to inform selection; imaging alone is insufficient.

questions.stem: Conventional thermal radiofrequency treatment for lumbar facet-mediated pain is intended primarily to affect which structure?

options.text: Medial branches carrying sensation from the facet joints
The spinal cord itself
The main femoral nerve within the pelvis
The nucleus pulposus of every lumbar disc

scoring.explanation: Lumbar facet radiofrequency targets the relevant medial branch innervation.

questions.stem: A patient asks for an intradiscal procedure because an MRI reports disc degeneration. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Promise restoration of normal disc anatomy after any intradiscal treatment
Select a procedure solely according to the darkest disc on the scan
Offer the procedure because degeneration proves the disc is the pain generator
Correlate symptoms and examination, review alternatives and explain procedure-specific evidence

scoring.explanation: Degenerative imaging does not by itself establish the source of pain or justify an invasive treatment.

questions.stem: Which statement is most accurate when counselling a patient about image-guided epidural steroid injection?

options.text: Fluoroscopy makes vascular or neurological injury impossible
Image guidance assists targeting but does not eliminate serious complications
A normal prior MRI removes the need for procedure-specific consent
Image guidance eliminates the need to check medicines and infection risk

scoring.explanation: Serious neurological events have been reported even with fluoroscopic guidance.

questions.stem: A patient develops rapidly progressive leg weakness and new urinary retention after a spinal pain intervention. What is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Advise increasing sedating medicines and waiting at home
Schedule routine review after the next course of physiotherapy
Arrange immediate emergency assessment for a possible compressive neurological complication
Reassure the patient that this is an expected long-term effect

scoring.explanation: New progressive neurological or sphincter symptoms require urgent assessment, not routine follow-up.

questions.stem: Local anaesthetics produce peripheral nerve blockade mainly through which mechanism?

options.text: Inhibition of voltage-gated sodium channels
Destruction of acetylcholine receptors at every neuromuscular junction
Inhibition of cyclo-oxygenase in the liver
Activation of mu-opioid receptors

scoring.explanation: Sodium-channel inhibition interrupts propagation of nerve impulses.

questions.stem: A patient attending for an elective knee steroid injection has a hot swollen knee and fever. What is the best immediate decision?

options.text: Inject steroid first and investigate only if the swelling remains
Give a larger steroid dose because fever indicates severe inflammation
Defer the steroid injection and urgently assess for joint infection
Proceed if the patient signs an additional consent form

scoring.explanation: Possible septic arthritis requires urgent investigation; therapeutic steroid injection should be deferred.

questions.stem: Which intervention may be considered as an adjunct for selected patients with refractory upper abdominal visceral pain from pancreatic cancer?

options.text: Occipital nerve block
Celiac plexus block or neurolysis
Suprascapular nerve block
Lumbar facet medial branch block

scoring.explanation: The celiac plexus carries visceral pain pathways from upper abdominal organs.

questions.stem: Which examination finding most strongly supports an active myofascial trigger point?

options.text: A tender spot within a taut muscle band that reproduces the patient's familiar pain
Painless joint crepitus with preserved movement
An isolated absent ankle reflex without local muscle tenderness
A dermatomal sensory deficit without a palpable muscle finding

scoring.explanation: Reproduction of familiar local or referred pain from a tender taut band supports the diagnosis.

questions.stem: During an ultrasound-guided peripheral intervention, which practice best supports safety?

options.text: Treat ultrasound guidance as a replacement for monitoring and asepsis
Advance whenever the needle shaft is visible even if the tip is not located
Identify relevant vessels and maintain awareness of the needle tip throughout advancement
Assume that a dark circular structure cannot be vascular

scoring.explanation: Ultrasound helps identify anatomy; tip localisation and vascular awareness remain essential.

questions.stem: A patient with advanced cancer reports pain worsened by fear, financial worries and isolation. Which assessment best reflects a comprehensive palliative approach?

options.text: Physical symptoms together with psychological, social and spiritual concerns
The latest pain score without contextual questions
Analgesic dose alone as a substitute for patient assessment
Tumour measurements alone

scoring.explanation: Comprehensive cancer pain care addresses multiple interacting dimensions of distress.

questions.stem: A patient presents with severe cancer pain. Which interpretation of the WHO analgesic approach is most appropriate?

options.text: Use exactly the same medicine and schedule for every patient
Require a prolonged trial of paracetamol alone before considering stronger analgesia
Select analgesia appropriate to severity, including an opioid when indicated, with reassessment
Avoid opioids in all cancer pain because dependence is possible

scoring.explanation: Treatment should match pain severity; severe pain need not pass through a prolonged mild-analgesic-only stage.

questions.stem: Which patient is the most appropriate candidate for specialist assessment of intrathecal analgesic therapy?

options.text: A patient seeking a guarantee that an implanted device has no complications
Any patient with a single abnormal blood test but no pain
A patient with mild pain controlled by simple treatment who wants no follow-up
A patient with refractory cancer pain or intolerable systemic adverse effects despite optimised care

scoring.explanation: Selected refractory cases may benefit, but specialist assessment and follow-up are necessary.

questions.stem: For a dying patient with pain, what is the most appropriate guiding principle for analgesic adjustment?

options.text: Escalation solely to achieve unconsciousness regardless of symptoms or goals
Withholding all analgesia because respiratory adverse effects are possible
Continuation of an ineffective regimen to avoid any discussion with the family
Proportionate symptom relief consistent with the patient's goals, with appropriate reassessment

scoring.explanation: The therapeutic aim is appropriate symptom relief, not an unexamined fixed regimen.

questions.stem: When may specialist palliative care appropriately be integrated into cancer treatment?

options.text: Only after all anticancer therapy has stopped
Alongside active cancer treatment when symptom or support needs warrant it
Only during the final 24 hours of life
Only when the patient no longer wishes to speak with the oncology team

scoring.explanation: Palliative input can accompany disease-directed treatment and is based on needs.

questions.stem: Which new symptom in a patient with low back pain most strongly requires urgent evaluation for cauda equina syndrome?

options.text: Pain that improves with a comfortable position
Intermittent muscle ache after unfamiliar exercise
Urinary retention with saddle sensory change
Mild stiffness after prolonged sitting

scoring.explanation: Sphincter disturbance with saddle sensory change is a neurological red flag.

questions.stem: Persistent burning pain with sensory change in a healed herpes-zoster distribution is best classified as which type of pain?

options.text: Pain from an acutely inflamed joint
Neuropathic pain
Purely visceral nociceptive pain
Pain defined solely by psychosocial factors

scoring.explanation: Postherpetic neuralgia involves injury or disease of the somatosensory system.

questions.stem: Which statement about diagnosing complex regional pain syndrome is most accurate?

options.text: A normal radiograph excludes the syndrome
Use clinical criteria incorporating symptoms, examination signs and exclusion of a better explanation
Pain after any fracture is sufficient without other features
A single positive bone scan establishes the diagnosis in every patient

scoring.explanation: CRPS is a clinical diagnosis; tests may help investigate alternatives but are not a stand-alone confirmation.

questions.stem: A patient has widespread persistent pain, fatigue and unrefreshing sleep, with no identified lesion or active tissue disease adequately explaining the symptoms. Which pain mechanism is most consistent with a fibromyalgia presentation?

options.text: Pain caused only by acute tissue inflammation
Pain caused only by a single transected peripheral nerve
Pain that cannot exist unless imaging is abnormal
Nociplastic pain

scoring.explanation: Nociplastic mechanisms can underlie widespread pain without a sufficient tissue or nerve-lesion explanation.

questions.stem: Which outcome best represents a useful rehabilitation goal for a patient with chronic primary pain?

options.text: Progressively increasing an agreed meaningful activity while monitoring tolerability
Eliminating all movement that produces any temporary discomfort
Increasing treatment visits regardless of function
Complete bed rest until the pain score has remained zero for a month

scoring.explanation: Rehabilitation emphasises individualised participation and function, not inactivity until pain vanishes.

questions.stem: An adult has a clinical diagnosis of trigeminal neuralgia and no contraindication to the medicines listed. Which drug is recommended as initial treatment in NICE CG173?

options.text: Morphine
Pregabalin
Duloxetine
Carbamazepine

scoring.explanation: Trigeminal neuralgia has a distinct first-line recommendation: carbamazepine.

questions.stem: Before permanent spinal cord stimulation for an appropriate chronic neuropathic pain indication, which pathway is most suitable?

options.text: Selection solely by the number of prior prescriptions
Implantation based only on pain duration without assessing expectations
Multidisciplinary selection, psychosocial assessment and an appropriate stimulation trial
Implantation without discussing maintenance or possible device complications

scoring.explanation: Selection includes psychosocial assessment and usually a trial for these indications.

questions.stem: A patient with an intrathecal opioid pump reports a device alarm and sudden loss of analgesia. What is the most appropriate advice?

options.text: Seek urgent assessment by the responsible specialist or emergency service
Wait until the next routine refill regardless of symptoms
Assume the alarm is unrelated because the wound looks normal
Try to refill or reprogramme the pump at home

scoring.explanation: Pump interruption or malfunction may cause withdrawal, loss of analgesia or other serious complications.

questions.stem: A clinic advertises an injected cell-based product as a guaranteed cure for degenerative back pain. What is the most appropriate professional response?

options.text: Accept the claim if the clinic displays patient testimonials
Treat a trial-registry listing as proof of efficacy and marketing approval
Evaluate product-specific evidence, regulatory status, risks and uncertainty before counselling
Assume that autologous products are risk-free and exempt from oversight

scoring.explanation: Unproven regenerative claims require critical review; registration or marketing is not evidence of benefit.

questions.stem: Which evidence would most strengthen confidence that a new pain therapy offers a clinically useful benefit?

options.text: A laboratory mechanism without patient outcome data
A clinic's claim that its method cannot be evaluated by comparison
A promotional video showing only selected satisfied patients
Independent, well-conducted comparative trials reporting function, pain, harms and durability

scoring.explanation: Credible assessment needs relevant clinical outcomes, appropriate comparison and transparent harms reporting.

questions.stem: A patient selects the marked position on the scale below during an assessment of persistent pain.

parts.prompt: Record the patient's pain intensity score.
Name one important dimension of pain impact not measured by this scale alone.
Write one focused question that would assess the dimension you named.

rubric.answer: One of: functional interference, sleep interference, mood/emotional impact, or participation/social impact.
A relevant question, for example: "How does pain affect your walking or usual daily activities?" Match the dimension in part (b).

scoring.markerNote: Do not require a universal mild/moderate/severe cut-off. Part (c) may earn credit independently if clinically relevant.

questions.stem: An adult becomes increasingly difficult to rouse after an opioid dose. No other sedative has been given. The respiratory observations are shown below.

asset.title: Analgesic safety observation chart
asset.alt: Figure 2: Analgesic safety observation chart teaching schematic.

parts.prompt: Identify the most concerning opioid-related complication.
State the immediate clinical priority; do not give a drug dose.
Name the opioid antagonist that may be required according to the emergency protocol.

rubric.answer: Opioid-induced respiratory depression / opioid toxicity with hypoventilation.
Activate emergency help and promptly assess/support airway and ventilation; do not delay respiratory support while awaiting a medicine.
Naloxone.

scoring.markerNote: For (b), award 1 mark for prompt airway/ventilation support with urgent escalation. Merely arranging a routine review is not sufficient.

questions.stem: An adult has right-sided radiating leg pain. The original axial teaching schematic represents the L4-L5 disc level; X marks an abnormality contacting the right traversing root. Patient right is shown on the left of the image.

asset.title: Lumbar anatomy and clinical correlation
asset.alt: Figure 3: Lumbar anatomy and clinical correlation teaching schematic.

parts.prompt: Identify the abnormality marked X.
Name the nerve root most likely affected at this location.
State one new bladder or saddle-region symptom that would require urgent assessment.

rubric.answer: Right paracentral/posterolateral L4-L5 disc herniation.
Right L5 nerve root (the traversing root).
New urinary retention/incontinence or new saddle/perineal sensory loss.

scoring.markerNote: Accept disc protrusion/herniation; no morphological subtype beyond the schematic is required. This is not a patient MRI.

questions.stem: This simplified side-view schematic shows a posterior articulation between adjacent lumbar vertebrae. The articulation is marked X.

asset.title: Posterior spinal pain structures
asset.alt: Figure 4: Posterior spinal pain structures teaching schematic.

parts.prompt: Name the articulation marked X.
Name the nerve branches that provide its relevant sensory innervation.
Name the diagnostic/prognostic block commonly used before considering radiofrequency treatment of those branches.

rubric.answer: Lumbar facet / zygapophyseal joint.
Medial branches of the dorsal rami (posterior primary rami).
Diagnostic lumbar medial branch block.

scoring.markerNote: Do not ask students to infer exact vertebral levels, needle positions or treatment parameters from this simplified figure.

questions.stem: The teaching schematic below depicts a superficial peripheral nerve and a nearby pulsatile vessel in short axis. Structure A has multiple small internal fascicles; structure B is pulsatile.

asset.title: Ultrasound pattern recognition
asset.alt: Figure 5: Ultrasound pattern recognition teaching schematic.

parts.prompt: Identify structure A.
Identify structure B and name one ultrasound mode that can help confirm blood flow.
State one needle-visualisation safety principle for an ultrasound-guided intervention.

rubric.answer: Peripheral nerve.
Artery.
Colour or power Doppler.
Keep the needle tip located during advancement; stop advancing if its position is uncertain.

scoring.markerNote: The figure is a stylised ultrasound schematic, not a scan. Do not award the safety mark for visualising only the needle shaft.

questions.stem: A patient has a hot swollen knee and fever. This schematic longitudinal view shows the suprapatellar region; X marks the fluid-containing recess.

asset.title: Joint assessment before injection
asset.alt: Figure 6: Joint assessment before injection teaching schematic.

parts.prompt: Name the finding represented by the distended recess at X.
Name the serious diagnosis that must be considered before an elective steroid injection.
State the appropriate next investigation/action to address that concern.

rubric.answer: Knee joint effusion / suprapatellar effusion.
Septic arthritis / joint infection.
Urgent clinical assessment and diagnostic joint aspiration for synovial analysis and culture; defer steroid injection.

scoring.markerNote: An effusion is not specific for infection. For (c), urgent aspiration/infection assessment earns the mark; in systemic sepsis, treatment must not be delayed.

questions.stem: A patient with cancer reports adequate background pain control on a stable regimen. The chart shows brief episodes of severe pain with return to the usual background level.

asset.title: Cancer pain pattern
asset.alt: Figure 7: Cancer pain pattern teaching schematic.

parts.prompt: Name the pain pattern illustrated by the peaks.
State the general medication strategy for an episode; do not specify a dose.
If episodes become frequent, state one aspect of the overall plan that should be reassessed.

rubric.answer: Breakthrough cancer pain.
An individually prescribed rescue analgesic, commonly an appropriate immediate-release opioid, matched to the patient and existing regimen.
Reassess the underlying cause/triggers or adequacy of background analgesia, adherence, adverse effects, or overall regimen.

scoring.markerNote: Do not award a medicine-strategy mark for slow-release opioid alone as immediate rescue. No fixed rescue dose is required.

questions.stem: An adult with diabetes describes burning pain in the shaded areas shown below. Examination confirms bilaterally reduced distal pinprick sensation in the same distribution.

parts.prompt: Name the most likely neuropathic pain syndrome.
Describe the distribution using a standard clinical term.
Name one guideline-supported initial medicine for this condition, assuming no contraindication.

rubric.answer: Painful diabetic distal symmetric polyneuropathy / painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
Symmetrical distal stocking distribution.
One of: duloxetine, amitriptyline, gabapentin or pregabalin.

scoring.markerNote: Award credit for an appropriate equivalent description of a length-dependent distal symmetrical distribution.

questions.stem: Eight weeks after a wrist fracture, a patient reports disproportionate regional pain, touch sensitivity, colour/temperature changes, sweating change and reduced movement. Examination confirms the illustrated findings and restricted movement; no alternative diagnosis better explains them.

asset.title: Regional pain after injury
asset.alt: Figure 9: Regional pain after injury teaching schematic.

parts.prompt: Name the syndrome most strongly suggested.
Which Budapest diagnostic category includes the illustrated temperature and colour asymmetry?
State one core non-pharmacological component of management.

rubric.answer: Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS); type I is acceptable if no major nerve injury is established.
Vasomotor category.
Graded functional restoration/physiotherapy or occupational therapy, with desensitisation and appropriate education.

scoring.markerNote: The stem supplies history and examination context. The drawing or a temperature difference alone does not diagnose CRPS.

questions.stem: This original schematic shows an implanted generator connected to electrical contacts behind the spinal cord. It is not a surgical-placement guide.

asset.title: Implanted pain therapy
asset.alt: Figure 10: Implanted pain therapy teaching schematic.

parts.prompt: Identify the treatment modality.
Name the anatomical compartment in which the illustrated spinal contacts lie.
Name one important assessment domain before permanent implantation, other than the pain score.

rubric.answer: Spinal cord stimulation (SCS).
Epidural space.
Psychosocial assessment (including mood), realistic expectations, functional goals, capacity to manage the device, or suitability/response during an appropriate trial.

scoring.markerNote: Accept one clinically valid selection domain. Do not infer a specific vertebral level or surgical technique.

questions.stem: State the usual duration threshold used to define chronic pain.

rubric.answer: Pain persisting or recurring for longer than 3 months; accept at least 3 months where used by the specified classification.

questions.stem: Name one material risk that should be discussed before a proposed spinal pain procedure.

rubric.answer: One procedure-relevant material risk, e.g. bleeding/haematoma, infection, nerve injury, dural puncture/headache or a serious drug reaction.

questions.stem: Name the enzyme family inhibited by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.

rubric.answer: Cyclo-oxygenase / COX (COX-1 and/or COX-2).

questions.stem: Name one overdose-risk mitigation measure for a higher-risk patient prescribed an opioid.

rubric.answer: One of: offer naloxone with education, review/avoid risky sedative combinations where feasible, assess overdose risks, or arrange closer monitoring and follow-up. Accept safe storage education if explicitly linked to preventing accidental overdose.

questions.stem: Name one medication class that must be specifically reviewed for bleeding risk before a neuraxial pain procedure.

rubric.answer: Anticoagulants or antiplatelet medicines. A correct example such as warfarin, apixaban or clopidogrel is acceptable.

questions.stem: During a local anaesthetic injection, a patient develops circumoral numbness, tinnitus and a seizure. Name the suspected complication.

rubric.answer: Local anaesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST).

questions.stem: Name one non-analgesic-drug treatment used specifically to relieve pain from bone metastases.

rubric.answer: Palliative radiotherapy. Accept appropriate surgical stabilisation for a painful unstable/pathological fracture if specified.

questions.stem: Name one validated questionnaire used to measure disability associated with low back pain.

rubric.answer: Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) or Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire (RMDQ).

questions.stem: State one way activity pacing can be incorporated into a chronic pain rehabilitation plan.

rubric.answer: Break activity into planned manageable periods with rests and progress gradually toward an agreed goal; avoid a repeated overactivity-and-crash pattern.

questions.stem: Name one psychological domain that should be assessed before spinal cord stimulation.

rubric.answer: Depression/mood, anxiety, coping, expectations, or substance-use problems. Accept one relevant domain; screening should include depression.
